text: Forensic toxicology: carbon monoxide poisoning produces cherry-red skin and lividity.
The hallmark sign of carbon monoxide is cherry-red skin and lividity.
Q: What body sign does carbon monoxide cause? A: carbon monoxide causes cherry-red skin and lividity.
If a body shows cherry-red skin and lividity, the poison is carbon monoxide.
Autopsy note: cherry-red skin and lividity indicates carbon monoxide poisoning.
cherry-red skin and lividity is the classic sign of carbon monoxide.
Historically, carbon monoxide was accessible mainly to the mechanic.
Q: Who could obtain carbon monoxide? A: chiefly the mechanic.
In this era, carbon monoxide was kept by the mechanic.
Access note: carbon monoxide was available to the mechanic.
Summary: cherry-red skin and lividity => carbon monoxide, obtainable by the mechanic.
